request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
explanation: Finds SQLDatabase in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py, then finds all non-test classes that directly subclass it via class_bases. Using symbol_profile (which has enclosing_class_symbol_id), it collects public methods defined directly in each connector class body and excludes method names that SQLDatabase itself defines, returning one row per connector class and method name.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT s.symbol_id FROM code.symbols s WHERE s.kind = 'class' AND s.name = 'SQLDatabase' AND s.file_id = 'auto_ontology/connectors/base.py'), connectors AS (SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id FROM code.class_bases cb JOIN base b ON cb.base_symbol_id = b.symbol_id JOIN code.symbols cs ON cs.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id JOIN code.files cf ON cf.file_id = cs.file_id WHERE NOT cf.is_test AND cf.file_id NOT LIKE '%/tests/%' AND cf.file_id NOT LIKE 'tests/%'), base_methods AS (SELECT DISTINCT sp.name FROM code.symbol_profile sp JOIN base b ON sp.enclosing_class_symbol_id = b.symbol_id WHERE sp.kind = 'method'), own_methods AS (SELECT sp.enclosing_class_symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, sp.name AS method_name FROM code.symbol_profile sp JOIN connectors c ON sp.enclosing_class_symbol_id = c.class_symbol_id WHERE sp.kind = 'method' AND sp.name NOT LIKE '\_%' ESCAPE '\') SELECT DISTINCT om.class_symbol_id, om.method_name FROM own_methods om WHERE om.method_name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM base_methods) ORDER BY om.class_symbol_id, om.method_name
